title: Presubmit bootstrapping and dependency "bonsai" trimming for faster CI feedback
author: Alana Rivera
release_notes: Presubmit performance: faster cold-start of lint/test runners and deterministic dependency trimming heuristics. Non-breaking internal developer tooling change.
description:
Context: Developers reported presubmit iterations taking 6-10 minutes for small JS/TS changes due to full toolchain install + global lint cache misses.
This PR introduces a two-part change we call 'presubmit bonsai': (1) a light bootstrapping path that installs a minimal, pinned toolset and warms a per-repo cache before heavier steps; (2) a deterministic dependency trimmer that prunes devdeps that are not referenced by changed files for the presubmit lane.
Motivation: reduce median feedback time on PRs while preserving correctness and making CI outcomes reproducible.
Summary of changes and approach:
- Add a new presubmit bootstrap action (ci/actions/presubmit-bootstrap.yml) that runs early in the pipeline. The action: installs node/go/python runtimes via our single-toolchain manifest, restores a compact cache key, and performs a minimal package.json/pyproject scan to produce a small dependency fingerprint.
- Implement dependency-trimmer service in tooling/dep-trimmer/: a lightweight, deterministic analyzer that uses glob-based change lists from git and static package manifest references to build a minimal devdeps subset for the presubmit job. It intentionally errs on the side of keeping more deps when uncertain to avoid flakiness.
- Split presubmit lanes: fastpath (lint + unit smoke) and fullpath (integration + heavy builds). The pipeline now runs fastpath first; if fastpath fails or a label requests full checks, the fullpath runs.
- Adjust cache strategy: introduce a cache warming step that populates the shared tooling cache with key components (node_modules partial tree, pip wheels) using the same keying algorithm across self-hosted and cloud runners.
- Add telemetry and tracing tags to the presubmit bootstrap so we can measure cold-start vs warmed runs.
Checklist:
- [x] New action implemented and documented
- [x] Dep-trimmer CLI and unit tests
- [x] Presubmit pipeline split and gating logic
- [x] Telemetry + alerting for increased failure rates
- [x] Load test on ephemeral runners (2k small PRs simulation)
Tests & validation performed:
- Local unit tests for dep-trimmer (100% pass)
- End-to-end night-run against a snapshot of 2k small PRs: median presubmit time reduced from 7m12s to 2m45s on warm cache; cold starts reduced from 6m34s to 3m10s.
- Ran canary on internal team repos for 72 hours. Observed a small uptick (+0.8%) in transient lint differences due to preserved devdeps trimming; rolled back an aggressive prune stage and added fallback to fullpath which resolved the noise.
Rollout plan:
- Step 1: enable presubmit-bonsai on internal repos (done)
- Step 2: enable opt-in for external OSS mirrors via repo flag for two weeks
- Step 3: full default rollout across org with monitoring and a 24h rollback window
Known limitations and mitigations:
- Dep-trimmer relies on static manifest references and will not detect runtime-loaded devdeps; mitigation: fallback to fullpath when uncertain and add an allowlist.
- Cache warmup increases storage write volume; mitigation: batched warmups and eviction policy.
Related: ENG-8421 (perf), ENG-8427 (deps hygiene).

review_comments: Marcus Holt: Can the dep-trimmer produce false negatives for monorepo cross-package refs? If so we should add an explicit flag to opt-out per repo.
Alana Rivera: It currently conservatively keeps deps when cross-package refs are detected. Added REPO_OPTOUT flag in the pipeline and documented fallback to fullpath.
Priya Shah: Suggest adding an integration test that simulates runtime-imported devdeps (e.g., require dynamic path).
Alana Rivera: Added a small integration harness and a test case that verifies fallback to fullpath when dynamic imports are detected.
Evan Liu: CI job logs show longer first-run time due to cache warmup; OK to proceed but add telemetry to monitor warmup amplification.

merge_outcome: Merged after two approvals. One transient e2e failure rerun resolved.
notes_for_operators: When rolling out, monitor presubmit_bootstrap.warmup_duration and presubmit_fastpath.failure_rate. If failure_rate > 1.5% for 30m, revert presubmit-bonsai flag and investigate dep-trimmer alerts.
